hints.title: Duplicate Subset Explosion Obstacle
hints.text: When elements repeat in nums, identical subsets appear at distinct recursion branches. How can sorting group duplicate items so that duplicate branches can be skipped at each depth?

hints.title: Sibling Level Skip Invariant
hints.text: Sort nums. In the loop at index i, if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1], skip i because the subset with that value was already explored by the prior sibling.

hints.title: Power Set Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: Sort nums. At every invocation, append a copy of current path to result. Loop i from start to len(nums) - 1. If i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1], continue. Append nums[i], recurse with i + 1, and pop.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10)
complexity.notes: At most 2^N subsets with O(N) cost to copy each subset into the result list.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^N subsets and filtering in a set causes redundant computation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Path buffer takes O(N) recursion memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sorting to allow instant sibling-level duplicate skipping.
